items.mnemonic: It's a window with the sun shining through it. A new DAY begins every time the sun peeks in. Say 'Nietzsche' (にち) was up all day.

examples.furigana: きょうはにちようびです。

items.mnemonic: A crescent MOON with two lines of clouds crossing it. One moon cycle = one MONTH. A 'gets' (げつ) glow at night.

examples.furigana: つきがきれいですね。
examples.en: The moon is beautiful, isn't it?

items.mnemonic: A central stream with droplets splashing on both sides. Imagine a 'sui'-cidal (すい) fish begging for WATER.

examples.furigana: みずをください。

items.mnemonic: Three peaks, the tallest in the middle. A MOUNTAIN named San (さん) towers over the valley.

examples.furigana: ふじさんはたかいです。

items.mnemonic: A PERSON walking on two legs. 'Jin' (じん) is a person who drinks gin.

examples.furigana: あのひとはせんせいです。

items.mnemonic: A PERSON (人) sits under a roof with a GOOD (良) meal. When food is good, you say 'sho-ku!' (しょく) and EAT.

examples.furigana: ちょうしょくをたべます。

items.mnemonic: Think 'Tabby cat' (た-べる) loves to EAT. The kanji 食 means eat; the okurigana べる makes it a verb.

examples.ja: 私はごはんを食べます。
examples.furigana: わたしはごはんをたべます。

items.mnemonic: A NOMad (のむ) in the desert needs to DRINK. The 食 radical on the left reminds you it's about consuming.

examples.furigana: みずをのみます。

items.mnemonic: Gachos (がっこう) – imagine kids fighting over a 'gotcha' toy at SCHOOL. 学 = study, 校 = school building.

examples.furigana: がっこうへいきます。

items.mnemonic: A TEACHER is someone who was born (生) before (先) you. Sensei = 'sen-say': the one who says what's up first.

examples.ja: 田中先生は優しいです。
examples.furigana: たなかせんせいはやさしいです。

items.mnemonic: Oh-oh, key! (おおきい) – a gigantic key so BIG it needs two hands. 大 looks like a person stretching their arms wide.

examples.furigana: おおきいいぬがいます。

items.mnemonic: Tom-o-dachi: your FRIEND Tom and his buddy Dachi hold hands (友 looks like two hands joining).

examples.furigana: ともだちとあそびます。

items.mnemonic: At the old STATION, horses (馬) were swapped. Say 'Eh? Key?' (えき) – 'Eh? Where's my ticket key?' at the STATION.

examples.furigana: えきはどこですか。

items.mnemonic: A person lying in bed (疒) with a fever. 'Byo-' (びょう) – a bee-yo-yo stings you and you get ILL.

examples.furigana: びょうきでやすみます。

items.mnemonic: A hill (阝) with a perfect (完) building on it: an INSTITUTION. 'In' (いん) – you go IN.

examples.furigana: びょういんにいきます。

items.mnemonic: An army (軍) on the move (辶) CARRIES supplies. 'Oon' (うん) – a lucky 'oon-der' truck delivers.

examples.furigana: にもつをはこびます。

items.mnemonic: You need power (力) to move something heavy (重). 'Doh!' (どう) – you drop it as you MOVE it.

examples.furigana: くるまがうごきます。

items.mnemonic: 病 (illness) + 院 (institution) = an institution for the ill: a HOSPITAL.

examples.furigana: びょういんではたらいています。

items.mnemonic: 運 (carry) + 動 (move) – carrying and moving your body: EXERCISE. 'Oon-doh!' – a workout grunt.

examples.furigana: まいあさうんどうします。

items.mnemonic: 'Yaku-soku' – a yak that's SO cute promised to be tied (束 = bundle) to you. A PROMISE binds like a bundle.

examples.ja: 友達と約束があります。
examples.furigana: ともだちとやくそくがあります。
examples.en: I have plans with a friend.

items.mnemonic: A 'June bee' (じゅんび) prepares honey all spring – that's PREPARATION. 備 = equip.

examples.furigana: りょこうのじゅんびをします。

items.mnemonic: Threads (糸) pass through the loom, year after year. A 'kay' (けい) thread PASSES THROUGH.

examples.furigana: じかんがたちました。

items.mnemonic: Water (氵) evenly (斉) poured SETTLES the dust. Once it's settled, it's FINISHED (すむ).

examples.furigana: しゅくだいがすみました。

items.mnemonic: Doing what's correct (正) by tapping with a stick (攵): the heavy hand of GOVERNMENT. 'Say!' (せい) – the leader speaks.

examples.furigana: せいふがはっぴょうしました。

items.mnemonic: Water (氵) on a platform (台) – a ruler controls floods to RULE; a doctor with water CURES.

examples.furigana: びょうきがなおりました。

items.mnemonic: 経 (pass through) + 済 (settle): money passes through hands and gets settled – the ECONOMY. 'Kay-zai'.

examples.ja: 経済が成長しています。
examples.furigana: けいざいがせいちょうしています。

items.mnemonic: 政 (government) + 治 (rule) = POLITICS. 'Say-G' – politicians always have something to say.

examples.ja: 政治に興味があります。
examples.furigana: せいじにきょうみがあります。

items.mnemonic: 経 (pass through) + 験 (test): things you've passed through and tested = EXPERIENCE. 'Kay-ken' – Ken has lots of it.

examples.ja: いい経験になりました。
examples.furigana: いいけいけんになりました。

items.mnemonic: 習 (learn) + 慣 (get used to) = HABIT. 'Shoo, can!' – you shoo away a can again and again until it's a HABIT.

examples.ja: 早起きの習慣があります。
examples.furigana: はやおきのしゅうかんがあります。
examples.en: I have a habit of getting up early.

items.mnemonic: A dog (犬) next to a bed-like board (爿): you check on the dog's CONDITION. 'Joe' (じょう) looks fine.

examples.furigana: じょうたいがいいです。

items.mnemonic: Your big brother (兄) beside the water (氵) reports on the SITUATION. 'Kyo' (きょう) – today's situation.

examples.furigana: じょうきょうをせつめいします。

items.mnemonic: A sheep (羊) offered up by 'me' (我) as a righteous sacrifice – JUSTICE. 'Ghee' (ぎ) is a pure, righteous butter.

examples.ja: 正義のために戦います。
examples.furigana: せいぎのためにたたかいます。

items.mnemonic: Hands (手) cradle something and say 'Shoh!' (しょう) – you ACKNOWLEDGE and receive a message.

examples.furigana: しょうにんをおねがいします。

items.mnemonic: 状 (condition) + 況 (situation) – a double dose of 'how things stand'. 'Joe, Kyo?' – 'Joe, what's the situation, Kyo?'

examples.ja: 現在の状況は厳しいです。
examples.furigana: げんざいのじょうきょうはきびしいです。

items.mnemonic: 意 (intention) + 義 (justice): the SIGNIFICANCE of an act is the justice behind it. 'Ee-ghee' – 'Eek, ghee is significant!'

examples.ja: この仕事には意義があります。
examples.furigana: このしごとにはいぎがあります。

items.mnemonic: 承 (receive) + 知 (know): you received it and know it – 'Understood!' Say 'Show, chee!' as you nod.

examples.furigana: しょうちしました。

items.mnemonic: 改 (reform) + 善 (good) = making things good by reforming – IMPROVEMENT. 'Kai-zen': Toyota's famous philosophy!

examples.ja: サービスを改善します。
examples.furigana: さーびすをかいぜんします。

items.mnemonic: A head (頁) heavy with heart (心) trudging slowly (夂): MELANCHOLY. 'You!' (ゆう) – you are the cause of my worry.

examples.furigana: しょうらいをうれえる。

items.mnemonic: The sun (日) behind love (愛) – love is blurry, OBSCURE. 'Eye' (あい) can't see clearly.

examples.furigana: あいまいなへんじ。

items.mnemonic: The sun (日) hasn't yet (未) risen – it's DARK. 'My' (まい) eyes can't see anything.

examples.furigana: ざんまいのひび。

items.mnemonic: A heart (忄) that falls (隋) away from effort: IDLE. 'Da!' – 'Da, I don't want to work.'

examples.furigana: だみんをむさぼる。

items.mnemonic: 曖 (obscure) + 昧 (dim) – doubly dim: AMBIGUOUS. 'Eye, my eye!' – you can't see clearly.

examples.ja: 曖昧な答えは困ります。
examples.furigana: あいまいなこたえはこまります。
examples.en: A vague answer is a problem.

items.mnemonic: 憂 (grief) + 鬱 (gloom, a dense thicket of strokes): the heavy feeling of MELANCHOLY. 'You, ooh, tsu…' – a sigh.

examples.furigana: げつようびはゆううつです。

items.mnemonic: 怠 (neglect) + 惰 (idle) – 'Tie, da!' – tied to the couch, totally idle: LAZINESS.

examples.furigana: たいだなせいかつをおくる。

items.mnemonic: Both kanji have a hand (扌) – you literally GRASP something with your hand. 'Ha, ah, ku!' – the 'aha!' moment.

examples.furigana: じょうきょうをはあくする。

grammar.formation: Verb て-form + もいい (+ ですか for a question)
grammar.notes: Ask permission with 〜てもいいですか and grant it with 〜てもいいです. Refuse with 〜てはいけません.

reviews.blankIndex: 使う (つかう) → て-form + もいい
reviews.correctKana: つかってもいい|使ってもいい

reviews.blankIndex: 撮る (とる) → て-form + もいい
reviews.correctKana: とってもいい|撮ってもいい
reviews.translationEn: May I take a photo here?

grammar.notes: Describes an action in progress or a continuing state, such as where someone lives.

reviews.blankIndex: 読む (よむ) → て-form + います
reviews.correctKana: よんでいます|読んでいます
reviews.translationEn: He is reading a book now.

reviews.blankIndex: 住む (すむ) → て-form + います
reviews.correctKana: すんでいます|住んでいます

grammar.notes: Expresses the speaker's own desire. It conjugates like an い-adjective: たくない, たかった.

reviews.blankIndex: 行く (いく) → ます-stem + たい
reviews.translationEn: I want to go to Japan.

reviews.blankIndex: 飲む (のむ) → ます-stem + たい
reviews.translationEn: I want to drink cold water.

grammar.formation: Verb ない-form (drop い) + ければなりません
grammar.notes: Expresses obligation. Casual forms: 〜なきゃ, 〜なければならない.

reviews.blankIndex: 起きる (おきる) → ない-form + ければなりません
reviews.correctKana: おきなければなりません|起きなければなりません
reviews.translationEn: I have to get up early tomorrow.

grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができる
grammar.notes: More formal than the potential form. Can also follow a noun-like action phrase.

grammar.meaning: Try to ~ / Make an effort to ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary / ない-form + ようにする
grammar.notes: Describes a continuous effort to do (or not do) something.

reviews.blankIndex: ようにする → ています
reviews.translationEn: I try to eat vegetables every day.

grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem / い-adj (drop い) / な-adj + そうだ
grammar.notes: Visual judgement based on appearance. Different from hearsay そうだ (I heard that).

reviews.blankIndex: い-adjective → drop い + そう + polite copula

grammar.formation: Verb て-form + ばかりいる
grammar.notes: Often carries a negative nuance of criticism.

reviews.blankIndex: 遊ぶ (あそぶ) → て-form + ばかりいる
reviews.correctKana: あそんでばかりいる|遊んでばかりいる
reviews.translationEn: He does nothing but play games.

grammar.meaning: Can't afford to ~ / Cannot (for social or moral reasons)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + わけにはいかない
grammar.notes: Expresses that circumstances make it impossible to do something. The negative-verb version means 'must do'.

reviews.sentenceJa: 明日試験があるから、今夜は遊ぶ＿＿＿＿＿。
reviews.blankIndex: わけ + には + いかない
reviews.translationEn: I can't play tonight because I have an exam tomorrow.

grammar.formation: Noun / Verb plain form + にもかかわらず
grammar.notes: Formal. な-adjective and noun may take である before it.

reviews.translationEn: Despite the rain, the match was held.

grammar.formation: Verb ない-stem + ざるを得ない (する → せざるを得ない)
grammar.notes: Literary and formal. Expresses reluctant necessity.

reviews.sentenceJa: 上司の命令なので、行か＿＿＿＿＿。
reviews.blankIndex: ない-stem + ざるを得ない
reviews.correctKana: ざるをえない|ざるを得ない
reviews.translationEn: Since it's the boss's order, I have no choice but to go.

grammar.formation: Verb ない-stem + ずにはいられない (する → せずにはいられない)
grammar.notes: Spontaneous, emotion-driven action that the speaker cannot resist.

reviews.blankIndex: ない-stem + ずにはいられなかった
reviews.correctKana: ずにはいられなかった
reviews.translationEn: Watching that movie, I couldn't help crying.

grammar.formation: Noun + をものともせず(に)
grammar.notes: Used to praise someone who pushes ahead in spite of obstacles.

reviews.blankIndex: noun + particle + ものともせず
reviews.correctKana: をものともせず|をものともせずに
reviews.translationEn: He pressed on, undeterred by the difficulties.
